questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070210/assets/2f847a5551c0bdc5aea20673814ba6eddc10daca7661cca2b2db76c953672225.png)

A plate occupies the region $D$ enclosed by the $y$-axis and the lines $x=y-1$ and $x=7-y$, as shown above. The mass density function of the plate is $\lambda (x,y)=\frac{y-1}{9}.$ Find the moment of inertia of the plate about the line $x=3.$
questions.worked_solution:
The moment of inertia of a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ about an axis of rotation $l$ is given by

$$
{I}_{l}={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda (x,y)$ is the mass density function of the lamina, and $r(x,y)$ is the distance from the line $l$ to the point $(x,y)$ on $D.$

First, notice that $D$ is a type I region with representation

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 3,\,\,x+1\le y\le 7-x},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070210/assets/b86b9a595786e544159e08fef12952c88e1bf9f796fb4ae3089e877dc9119b3f.png)

The distance between a point on $D$ and the line $x=3$ is given by

$$
r(x,y)=|x-3|
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the line $x=3$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}I & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{x+1}^{7-x}(\frac{y-1}{9})|x-3{|}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{x+1}^{7-x}(\frac{y-1}{9})(x-3)^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}(x-3)^{2}[{\int }_{x+1}^{7-x}\frac{y-1}{9}\,\text{d}y]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}(x-3)^{2}{[\frac{(y-1)^{2}}{18}]}_{x+1}^{7-x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}(x-3)^{2}[\frac{(6-x)^{2}}{18}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{18}]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}(x-3)^{2}[\frac{12(3-x)}{18}]\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{2}{3}{\int }_{0}^{3}(x-3)^{3}\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{2}{3}{[\frac{(x-3)^{4}}{4}]}_{0}^{3} \\  & =-\frac{2}{3}(0-\frac{81}{4}) \\  & =\frac{27}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
A rectangular plate occupies the region
$D={(x,y)\,:\,1\le x\le 3,\,\,0\le y\le 1}$
with mass density function $\lambda (x,y)=x+y-1$ Find the moment of inertia of this plate about the line $x=2.$
questions.worked_solution:
The moment of inertia of a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ about an axis of rotation $l$ is given by

$$
{I}_{l}={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda (x,y)$ is the mass density function of the lamina, and $r(x,y)$ is the distance from the line $l$ to the point $(x,y)$ on $D.$

The distance between a point on $D$ and the line $x=2$ is given by

$$
r(x,y)=|x-2|.
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the line $x=2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{l} & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{1}(x+y-1)|x-2{|}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{1}(x-2+y+1)(x-2)^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{1}(x-2)^{3}+(y+1)(x-2)^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}{[y(x-2)^{3}+\frac{1}{2}(y+1)^{2}(x-2)^{2}]}_{0}^{1}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}(x-2)^{3}+\frac{3}{2}(x-2)^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{(x-2)^{4}}{4}+\frac{(x-2)^{3}}{2}]}_{1}^{3} \\  & =(\frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{2})-(\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =\frac{3}{4}+\frac{1}{4} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
A rectangular plate occupies the region
$D={(x,y)\,:\,-2\le x\le 1,\,\,1\le y\le 2}$
with mass density function $\lambda (x,y)=y-x.$ Find the moment of inertia of this plate about the line $x=-2.$
questions.worked_solution:
The moment of inertia of a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ about an axis of rotation $l$ is given by

$$
{I}_{l}={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda (x,y)$ is the mass density function of the lamina, and $r(x,y)$ is the distance from the line $l$ to the point $(x,y)$ on $D.$

The distance between a point on $D$ and the line $x=-2$ is given by

$$
r(x,y)=|x-(-2)|=|x+2|.
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the line $x=-2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{l} & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{2}(y-x)|x+2{|}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{2}(y-x)(x+2)^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{2}y(x+2)^{2}-x(x+2)^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{1}{[\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}(x+2)^{2}-xy(x+2)^{2}]}_{1}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-2}^{1}(3-2x)(x+2)^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-2}^{1}(-2{x}^{3}-5{x}^{2}+4x+12)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{[\frac{-{x}^{4}}{2}-\frac{5{x}^{3}}{3}+2{x}^{2}+12x]}_{-2}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}((-\frac{1}{2}-\frac{5}{3}+2+12)-(-8+\frac{40}{3}+8-24)) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}((14-\frac{13}{6})-(-24+\frac{40}{3})) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\frac{135}{6}) \\  & =\frac{45}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

A plate occupies the region $D$ enclosed by the $y$-axis and the lines $x=2y$ and $x=3-y$, as shown above. The mass density function of the plate is $\lambda (x,y)=\frac{y}{6}.$ Find the moment of inertia of the plate about the line $x=2.$
questions.worked_solution:
The moment of inertia of a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ about an axis of rotation $l$ is given by

$$
{I}_{l}={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda (x,y)$ is the mass density function of the lamina, and $r(x,y)$ is the distance from the line $l$ to the point $(x,y)$ on $D.$

First, notice that $D$ is a type I region with representation

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,\,\frac{x}{2}\le y\le 3-x},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070210/assets/0c9efcbae53bdd2620b0bf7009ce4f4f2a20a38f393cac008899621ec391d261.png)

The distance between a point on $D$ and the line $x=2$ is given by

$$
r(x,y)=|x-2|
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the line $x=2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}I & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{x/2}^{3-x}(\frac{y}{6})|x-2{|}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{x/2}^{3-x}(\frac{y}{6})(x-2)^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}({x}^{2}-4x+4)[{\int }_{x/2}^{3-x}\frac{y}{6}\,\text{d}y]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}({x}^{2}-4x+4){[\frac{{y}^{2}}{12}]}_{x/2}^{3-x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}({x}^{2}-4x+4)[\frac{(3-x)^{2}}{12}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{48}]\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{48}{\int }_{0}^{2}({x}^{2}-4x+4)(36-24x+3{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{48}{\int }_{0}^{2}3{x}^{4}-36{x}^{3}+144{x}^{2}-240x+144\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{{x}^{5}}{80}-\frac{3{x}^{4}}{16}+{x}^{3}-\frac{5{x}^{2}}{2}+3x]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =(\frac{2}{5}-3+8-10+6)-0 \\  & =\frac{7}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

A plate occupies the region $D$ enclosed by the $y$-axis and the lines $x=\frac{4y}{3}$ and $x=4-\frac{4y}{3}$, as shown above. The mass density function of the plate is $\lambda (x,y)=2-x.$ Find the moment of inertia of the plate about the line $x=2.$
questions.worked_solution:
The moment of inertia of a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ about an axis of rotation $l$ is given by

$$
{I}_{l}={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda (x,y)$ is the mass density function of the lamina, and $r(x,y)$ is the distance from the line $l$ to the point $(x,y)$ on $D.$

First, notice that $D$ is a type I region with representation

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,\,\frac{3}{4}x\le y\le 3-\frac{3}{4}x},
$$

 

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070210/assets/1f332ebf554ac0e1b9e5099244aa50de0beef38c92efcba04e95e73abd21ecb6.png)

    

The distance between a point on $D$ and the line $x=2$ is given by

$$
r(x,y)=|x-2|
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the line $x=2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}I & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{3x/4}^{3-3x/4}(2-x)|x-2{|}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{3x/4}^{3-3x/4}{(2-x)}^{3}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(2-x)^{3}[{\int }_{3x/4}^{3-3x/4}\,\text{d}y]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(2-x)^{3}[y]_{3x/4}^{3-3x/4}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(2-x)^{3}(3-\frac{3x}{4}-\frac{3x}{4})\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}(2-x)^{4}\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{3}{2}{[\frac{(2-x)^{5}}{5}]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =-\frac{3}{2}(0-\frac{{2}^{5}}{5}) \\  & =\frac{48}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070210/assets/ed4f595e7613254fd0cb8f27cf0b0f7443cfbe382ab525b0ca8d527c07f528fd.png)

A plate with mass $M$ and uniform mass density occupies the region $D$ enclosed between the curves $y={x}^{2}$ and $y=\sqrt{x}$, as shown above. Given that the region has an area of $\frac{1}{3},$ find the moment of inertia of the plate about the line $x=1.$
questions.worked_solution:
The moment of inertia of a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ about an axis of rotation $l$ is given by

$$
{I}_{l}={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda (x,y)$ is the mass density function of the lamina, and $r(x,y)$ is the distance from the line $l$ to the point $(x,y)$ on $D.$

First, notice that $D$ is a type I region with representation

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,{x}^{2}\le y\le \sqrt{x}},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070210/assets/60ec523346df73503dd61893994de6ec31069271b1157f153bbe988c9e694798.png)

The distance between a point on $D$ and the line $x=1$ is given by

$$
r(x,y)=|x-1|.
$$

Since the plate has uniform density, the mass density function is given by

$$
\lambda (x,y)=\frac{M}{A}=3M.
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the line $x=1$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}I & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & =3M{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{\sqrt{x}}|x-1{|}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =3M{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{\sqrt{x}}(x-1)^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =3M{\int }_{0}^{1}(x-1)^{2}[y]_{y={x}^{2}}^{y=\sqrt{x}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =3M{\int }_{0}^{1}({x}^{2}-2x+1)(\sqrt{x}-{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & =3M{\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{5/2}-2{x}^{3/2}+{x}^{1/2}-{x}^{4}+2{x}^{3}-{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =3M{[\frac{2}{7}{x}^{7/2}-\frac{4}{5}{x}^{5/2}+\frac{2}{3}{x}^{3/2}-\frac{1}{5}{x}^{5}+\frac{1}{2}{x}^{4}-\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =3M(\frac{2}{7}-\frac{4}{5}+\frac{2}{3}-\frac{1}{5}+\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{3}-0) \\  & =\frac{5M}{14}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
A rectangular plate of mass $M$ and uniform mass density occupies the region
$D={(x,y)\,:\,-1\le x\le 2,\,\,0\le y\le 2}.$
Find the moment of inertia of this plate about the line $x=-1.$
questions.worked_solution:
The moment of inertia of a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ about an axis of rotation $l$ is given by

$$
{I}_{l}={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda (x,y)$ is the mass density function of the lamina, and $r(x,y)$ is the distance from the line $l$ to the point $(x,y)$ on $D.$

First, the distance between a point on $D$ and the line $x=-1$ is given by

$$
r(x,y)=|x+1|.
$$

Next, the area of the rectangular plate $D$ is $A=3\cdot 2=6.$ Since the plate has uniform density, the mass density function is given by

$$
\lambda (x,y)=\frac{M}{A}=\frac{M}{6}.
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the line $x=-1$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{l} & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{2}\frac{M}{6}|x+1{|}^{2}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{2}\frac{M}{6}(x+1)^{2}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{M}{6}({\int }_{-1}^{2}(x+1)^{2}\,\text{d}x)({\int }_{0}^{2}\,\text{d}y) \\  & =\frac{M}{6}\cdot [\frac{1}{3}(x+1)^{3}]_{-1}^{2}\cdot [y]_{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{M}{6}(\frac{1}{3}(2+1)^{3}-\frac{1}{3}(-1+1)^{3})\cdot (2-0) \\  & =\frac{M}{6}(9-0)\cdot 2 \\  & =3M.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
A rectangular plate of mass $M$ and uniform mass density occupies the region
$D={(x,y)\,:\,2\le x\le 5,\,\,1\le y\le 2}.$
Find the moment of inertia of this plate about the line $x=2.$
questions.worked_solution:
The moment of inertia of a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ about an axis of rotation $l$ is given by

$$
{I}_{l}={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda (x,y)$ is the mass density function of the lamina, and $r(x,y)$ is the distance from the line $l$ to the point $(x,y)$ on $D.$

First, the distance between a point on $D$ and the line $x=2$ is given by

$$
r(x,y)=|x-2|.
$$

Next, the area of the rectangular plate $D$ is $A=3\cdot 1=3.$ Since the plate has uniform density, the mass density function is given by

$$
\lambda (x,y)=\frac{M}{A}=\frac{M}{3}.
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the line $x=2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{l} & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{2}^{5}\frac{M}{3}|x-2{|}^{2}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{2}^{5}\frac{M}{3}(x-2)^{2}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{M}{3}({\int }_{2}^{5}(x-2)^{2}\,\text{d}x)({\int }_{1}^{2}\,\text{d}y) \\  & =\frac{M}{3}\cdot [\frac{1}{3}(x-2)^{3}]_{2}^{5}\cdot {[y]}_{1}^{2} \\  & =\frac{M}{3}(\frac{1}{3}(5-2)^{3}-\frac{1}{3}(2-2)^{3})\cdot (2-1) \\  & =\frac{M}{3}(9-0)\cdot 1 \\  & =3M.\end{aligned}
$$

A rectangular plate of mass $M$ and uniform mass density occupies the region
$D={(x,y)\,:\,-1\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le 2}.$
Find the moment of inertia of this plate about the line $y=2.$
questions.worked_solution:
The moment of inertia of a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ about an axis of rotation $l$ is given by

$$
{I}_{l}={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda (x,y)$ is the mass density function of the lamina, and $r(x,y)$ is the distance from the line $l$ to the point $(x,y)$ on $D.$

First, the distance between a point on $D$ and the line $y=2$ is given by

$$
r(x,y)=|y-2|.
$$

Next, the area of the rectangular plate $D$ is $A=2\cdot 2=4.$ Since the plate has uniform density, the mass density function is given by

$$
\lambda (x,y)=\frac{M}{A}=\frac{M}{4}.
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the line $y=2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{l} & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{M}{4}|y-2{|}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{M}{4}(y-2)^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{M}{4}({\int }_{-1}^{1}\,\text{d}x)({\int }_{0}^{2}(y-2)^{2}\,\text{d}y) \\  & =\frac{M}{4}\cdot [x]_{-1}^{1}\cdot {[\frac{1}{3}(y-2)^{3}]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{M}{4}(1-(-1))(\frac{1}{3}(2-2)^{3}-\frac{1}{3}(0-2)^{3}) \\  & =\frac{M}{2}(0-(-\frac{8}{3})) \\  & =\frac{4M}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

A triangular plate with mass $M$ occupies the region $D$ enclosed between the $x$-axis and the lines $x=1$ and $y=2x.$
The mass density at each point is proportional to its distance from the $x$-axis. Find the moment of inertia of the plate about the line $x=-2.$
questions.worked_solution:
The moment of inertia of a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ about an axis of rotation $l$ is given by

$$
{I}_{l}={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda (x,y)$ is the mass density function of the lamina, and $r(x,y)$ is the distance from the line $l$ to the point $(x,y)$ on $D.$

First, notice that $D$ is a type I region with representation

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le 2x},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070210/assets/f040a5500a1415b8617300f34074bb16d895889354ed7e722dbd668a233daebb.png)

Also, the distance between a point and the line $x=-2$ is given by

$$
r(x,y)=|x-(-2)|=|x+2|.
$$

Next, the mass density can be written as $\lambda (x,y)=k|y|=ky,$ where $k$ is a constant of proportionality. We can find the value of $k$ by integrating the mass density function over the plate.

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2x}ky\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =k{\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{2x}y\,\text{d}y]\text{d}x \\  & =k{\int }_{0}^{1}{[\frac{1}{2}{y}^{2}]}_{0}^{2x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =k{\int }_{0}^{1}2{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =k\cdot {[\frac{2}{3}{x}^{3}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{2}{3}k.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, 

$$
\lambda (x,y)=ky=\frac{3M}{2}y.
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the line $x=-2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{l} & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2x}\frac{3M}{2}y\,|x+2{|}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2x}\frac{3M}{2}y(x+2)^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3M}{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}(x+2)^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{2x}y\,\text{d}y]\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3M}{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}(x+2)^{2}{[\frac{1}{2}{y}^{2}]}_{0}^{2x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3M}{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}2{x}^{2}(x+2)^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3M}{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}2{x}^{4}+8{x}^{3}+8{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3M}{2}{[\frac{2}{5}{x}^{5}+2{x}^{4}+\frac{8}{3}{x}^{3}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{3M}{2}[\frac{2}{5}+2+\frac{8}{3}-0] \\  & =\frac{3M}{2}[\frac{76}{15}] \\  & =\frac{38M}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
A rectangular plate of mass $M$ occupies the region
$D={(x,y)\,:\,-2\le x\le 2,\,\,0\le y\le 1}.$
The mass density at each point is proportional to the square of its distance from the $x$-axis. Find the moment of inertia of the plate about the line $y=2.$
questions.worked_solution:
The moment of inertia of a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ about an axis of rotation $l$ is given by

$$
{I}_{l}={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda (x,y)$ is the mass density function of the lamina, and $r(x,y)$ is the distance from the line $l$ to the point $(x,y)$ on $D.$

First, the distance between a point and the line $y=2$ is given by

$$
r(x,y)=|y-2|.
$$

Next, the mass density can be written as $\lambda (x,y)=k{y}^{2},$ where $k$ is a constant of proportionality. We can find the value of $k$ by integrating the mass density function over the plate.

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}k{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =k({\int }_{-2}^{2}\,\text{d}x)({\int }_{0}^{1}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y) \\  & =k\cdot [x]_{-2}^{2}\cdot {[\frac{1}{3}{y}^{3}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{k}{3}(2-(-2))(1-0) \\  & =\frac{4k}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, 

$$
\lambda (x,y)=k{y}^{2}=\frac{3M}{4}{y}^{2}.
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the line $y=2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{l} & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{3M}{4}{y}^{2}|y-2{|}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{3M}{4}{y}^{2}(y-2)^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3M}{4}({\int }_{-2}^{2}\,\text{d}x)({\int }_{0}^{1}({y}^{4}-4{y}^{3}+4{y}^{2})\,\text{d}y) \\  & =\frac{3M}{4}\cdot [x]_{-2}^{2}\cdot {[\frac{{y}^{5}}{5}-{y}^{4}+\frac{4{y}^{3}}{3}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{3M}{4}\cdot (2-(-2))\cdot (\frac{1}{5}-1+\frac{4}{3}) \\  & =\frac{3M}{4}\cdot 4\cdot \frac{8}{15} \\  & =\frac{8M}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

A plate with mass $M$ occupies the region $D$ enclosed between the curves $y={x}^{2}$ and $y=4$ in the first quadrant.
The mass density at each point is proportional to its distance from the $y$-axis. Find the moment of inertia of the plate about the line $y=2.$
questions.worked_solution:
The moment of inertia of a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ about an axis of rotation $l$ is given by

$$
{I}_{l}={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda (x,y)$ is the mass density function of the lamina, and $r(x,y)$ is the distance from the line $l$ to the point $(x,y)$ on $D.$

First, notice that $D$ is a type I region with representation

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,\,{x}^{2}\le y\le 2},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070210/assets/f5a73161415455032a7fd2031dba8f1c56a7ccb40bf6dc3e4fa405a69aee74d8.png)

Also, the distance between a point and the line $y=2$ is given by

$$
r(x,y)=|y-2|.
$$

Next, the mass density can be written as $\lambda (x,y)=k|x|=kx,$ where $k$ is a constant of proportionality. We can find the value of $k$ by integrating the mass density function over the plate.

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{4}kx\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =k{\int }_{0}^{2}x[y]_{{x}^{2}}^{4}\,\text{d}x \\  & =k{\int }_{0}^{2}x(4-{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & =k{\int }_{0}^{2}(4x-{x}^{3})\,\text{d}x \\  & =k{[2{x}^{2}-\frac{1}{4}{x}^{4}]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =k(8-4) \\  & =4k.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, 

$$
\lambda (x,y)=kx=\frac{M}{4}x.
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the line $y=2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{l} & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{4}\frac{M}{4}x\cdot |y-2{|}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{4}\frac{M}{4}x\cdot (y-2)^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{M}{4}{\int }_{0}^{2}x{[\frac{(y-2)^{3}}{3}]}_{{x}^{2}}^{4}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{M}{4}{\int }_{0}^{2}x(\frac{8}{3}-\frac{({x}^{2}-2)^{3}}{3})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{M}{12}{\int }_{0}^{2}(8x-x({x}^{2}-2)^{3})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{M}{12}{\int }_{0}^{2}(-{x}^{7}+6{x}^{5}-12{x}^{3}+16)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{M}{12}{[-\frac{{x}^{8}}{8}+{x}^{6}-3{x}^{4}+16x]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{M}{12}(-32+64-48+32) \\  & =\frac{4M}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

The mass density at each point is proportional to the square of its distance from the $y$-axis. Find the moment of inertia of the plate about the line $y=0.$
questions.worked_solution:
The moment of inertia of a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ about an axis of rotation $l$ is given by

$$
{I}_{l}={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda (x,y)$ is the mass density function of the lamina, and $r(x,y)$ is the distance from the line $l$ to the point $(x,y)$ on $D.$

First, notice that $D$ is a type I region with representation

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,\frac{x}{2}\le y\le x},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070210/assets/84ec89a3f4d786fe387b33aacc3de7c013866387354897f785ff69f9d65437ad.png)

Also, the distance between a point and the line $y=0$ is given by

$$
r(x,y)=|y|.
$$

Next, the mass density can be written as $\lambda (x,y)=k{x}^{2},$ where $k$ is a constant of proportionality. We can find the value of $k$ by integrating the mass density function over the plate.

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{x/2}^{x}k{x}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =k{\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{x/2}^{x}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}y]\text{d}x \\  & =k{\int }_{0}^{1}{[{x}^{2}y]}_{x/2}^{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =k{\int }_{0}^{1}({x}^{3}-\frac{{x}^{3}}{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & =k{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{{x}^{3}}{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =k\cdot {[\frac{{x}^{4}}{8}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{k}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, 

$$
\lambda (x,y)=k{x}^{2}=8M{x}^{2}.
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the line $y=0$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{l} & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{x/2}^{x}8M{x}^{2}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =8M{\int }_{0}^{1}{[\frac{{x}^{2}{y}^{3}}{3}]}_{x/2}^{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =8M{\int }_{0}^{1}(\frac{{x}^{5}}{3}-\frac{{x}^{5}}{24})\,\text{d}x \\  & =8M{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{7{x}^{5}}{24}\,\text{d}x \\  & =M{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{7{x}^{5}}{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =M{[\frac{7{x}^{6}}{18}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{7M}{18}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
A rectangular plate of mass $M$ occupies the region
$D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,\,0\le y\le 3}.$
The mass density at each point is proportional to its $x$-coordinate. Find the moment of inertia of the plate about the line $y=-1.$
questions.worked_solution:
The moment of inertia of a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ about an axis of rotation $l$ is given by

$$
{I}_{l}={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda (x,y)$ is the mass density function of the lamina, and $r(x,y)$ is the distance from the line $l$ to the point $(x,y)$ on $D.$

First, the distance between a point and the line $y=-1$ is given by

$$
r(x,y)=|y+1|.
$$

Next, the mass density can be written as $\lambda (x,y)=kx,$ where $k$ is a constant of proportionality. We can find the value of $k$ by integrating the mass density function over the plate.

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{3}kx\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =k({\int }_{0}^{2}x\,\text{d}x)({\int }_{0}^{3}\,\text{d}y) \\  & =k\cdot {[\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}]}_{0}^{2}\cdot [y]_{0}^{3} \\  & =k(2-0)(3-0) \\  & =6k.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, 

$$
\lambda (x,y)=kx=\frac{M}{6}x.
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the line $y=-1$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{l} & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{3}\frac{M}{6}x|y+1{|}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{3}\frac{M}{6}x(y+1)^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{M}{6}({\int }_{0}^{2}x\,\text{d}x)({\int }_{0}^{3}(y+1)^{2}\,\text{d}y) \\  & =\frac{M}{6}\cdot {[\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}]}_{0}^{2}\cdot {[\frac{1}{3}(y+1)^{3}]}_{0}^{3} \\  & =\frac{M}{6}\cdot \frac{1}{2}(4-0)\cdot [\frac{1}{3}(64-1)] \\  & =\frac{M}{6}\cdot 2\cdot \frac{63}{3} \\  & =7M.\end{aligned}
$$

A plate occupies the region $D$ enclosed by the $y$-axis and the lines $x=\dfrac{y}2$ and $x=y-2$, as shown above. The mass density function of the plate is $\lambda(x,y) =\dfrac y8.$ Find the moment of inertia of the plate about the line $x=2.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The moment of inertia of a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ about an axis of rotation $l$ is given by

$$
I_l = \iint\limits_D \lambda (x,y) [r(x,y)]^2 \:\textrm{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda(x,y)$ is the mass density function of the lamina, and $r(x,y)$ is the distance from the line $l$ to the point $(x,y)$ on $D.$

First, notice that $D$ is a type I region with representation

$$
D = \left\{ (x,y) \: : \: 0 \leq x \leq 2, \:\: 2x \leq y \leq x+2 \right\},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070210/assets/69dcf02cc1883f2b04f81bd6dd486bbe24fedbb813db5778ae3b33ed1fb42e90.png)

     

The distance between a point on $D$ and the line $x=2$ is given by

$$
r(x,y) = |x - 2|.
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the line $x=2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}I & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{2x}^{x+2}(\frac{y}{8})|x-2{|}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{2x}^{x+2}(\frac{y}{8})(x-2)^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(x-2)^{2}{\int }_{2x}^{x+2}\frac{y}{8}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(x-2)^{2}{[\frac{{y}^{2}}{16}]}_{2x}^{x+2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{16}{\int }_{0}^{2}(x-2)^{2}((x+2)^{2}-(2x)^{2})\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{16}{\int }_{0}^{2}({x}^{2}-4x+4)(4+4x-3{x}^{2})\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{16}{\int }_{0}^{2}(16-24{x}^{2}+16{x}^{3}-3{x}^{4})\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{16}{[16x-8{x}^{3}+4{x}^{4}-\frac{3{x}^{5}}{5}]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{16}(32-64+64-\frac{96}{5})-0 \\  & =\frac{1}{16}(\frac{64}{5}) \\  & =\frac{4}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The moment of inertia of a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ about an axis of rotation $l$ is given by

$$
I_l = \iint\limits_D \lambda (x,y) [r(x,y)]^2 \:\textrm{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda(x,y)$ is the mass density function of the lamina, and $r(x,y)$ is the distance from the line $l$ to the point $(x,y)$ on $D.$

First, notice that $D$ is a type I region with representation

$$
D = \left\{ (x,y) \: : \: 0 \leq x \leq 3, \:\: x \leq y \leq 4x-x^2 \right\},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070210/assets/6291950b5483f3c102df7249674412c7c11646409cb1b43df604de6bd5ace86f.png)

  

The distance between a point on $D$ and the line $x=3$ is given by

$$
r(x,y) = |x - 3|.
$$

Since the plate has uniform density, the mass density function is given by

$$
\lambda(x,y) = \dfrac{M}{\mathcal{A}} = \dfrac{2M}{9}.
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the line $x=3$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}I & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & =\frac{2M}{9}{\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{x}^{4x-{x}^{2}}|x-3{|}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{2M}{9}{\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{x}^{4x-{x}^{2}}(x-3)^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{2M}{9}{\int }_{0}^{3}(x-3)^{2}[y]_{y=x}^{y=4x-{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{2M}{9}{\int }_{0}^{3}({x}^{2}-6x+9)(3x-{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{2M}{9}{\int }_{0}^{3}-{x}^{4}+9{x}^{3}-27{x}^{2}+27x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{2M}{9}{[-\frac{{x}^{5}}{5}+\frac{9{x}^{4}}{4}-9{x}^{3}+\frac{27{x}^{2}}{2}]}_{0}^{3} \\  & =\frac{2M}{{3}^{2}}(-\frac{{3}^{5}}{5}+\frac{{3}^{6}}{4}-{3}^{5}+\frac{{3}^{5}}{2}) \\  & =2\cdot {3}^{3}M(-\frac{1}{5}+\frac{3}{4}-1+\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =\frac{27M}{10}.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The moment of inertia of a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ about an axis of rotation $l$ is given by

$$

where $\lambda(x,y)$ is the mass density function of the lamina, and $r(x,y)$ is the distance from the line $l$ to the point $(x,y)$ on $D.$

First, notice that $D$ is a type I region with representation

$$
D = \left\{ (x,y) \: : \: 0 \leq x \leq 1, \:\: 0 \leq y \leq \sqrt x \right\},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070210/assets/7faaecf39250dbdd1b92d789f6c217afe883c27533b563dae82ed82d228d9b4d.png)

$$

Next, the mass density can be written as $\lambda(x,y) = k |y| = ky,$ where $k$ is a constant of proportionality. We can find the value of $k$ by integrating the mass density function over the plate.

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{x}}ky\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =k{\int }_{0}^{1}{[\frac{1}{2}{y}^{2}]}_{0}^{\sqrt{x}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{k}{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}(x-0)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{k}{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{k}{2}\cdot {[\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{k}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\lambda(x,y) = k y = 4M y.
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{l} & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{x}}4My\,|x+1{|}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{x}}4My(x+1)^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =4M{\int }_{0}^{1}(x+1)^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{x}}y\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =4M{\int }_{0}^{1}(x+1)^{2}{[\frac{1}{2}{y}^{2}]}_{0}^{\sqrt{x}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2M{\int }_{0}^{1}(x+1)^{2}(x-0)\,\text{d}x \\  & =2M{\int }_{0}^{1}({x}^{3}+2{x}^{2}+x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =2M{[\frac{1}{4}{x}^{4}+\frac{2}{3}{x}^{3}+\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =2M(\frac{1}{4}+\frac{2}{3}+\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =2M\cdot \frac{17}{12} \\  & =\frac{17M}{6}.\end{aligned}
